# Validation study

How well Parity detects known faults and how often it wrongly flags correct deployments.
**Every number in the tables comes from `parity inject-faults run`** and is generated by
`scripts/update_result_docs.py` from raw files in [data/](data/); nothing is typed by hand.

Two studies are reported. The **v0.1.1 study** is current: it evaluates the frozen v0.1.1 code
on fresh evaluation data. The **v0.1.0 study** is kept unchanged, with its raw data, as the
historical record of the first release.

## v0.1.1 study

### How the evaluation was kept clean

* **Frozen code.** All v0.1.1 changes (result integrity, tools probe v2, harness changes) were
  committed and tagged `v0.1.1-rc1` before any evaluation run. The study ran from a separate
  checkout of that tag, so later development could not change it; every run manifest records the
  package's code fingerprint and every result row the study fingerprint
  ([data/v0.1.1-study-manifest.json](data/v0.1.1-study-manifest.json)).
* **Three disjoint kinds of data.**
  *Calibration*: one run each on the benign deployments `benign-gpu-p4` and `benign-cpu-p4`,
  made once and reused by every evaluation run (fingerprint in the manifest,
  [data/v0.1.1-calibration.json](data/v0.1.1-calibration.json)).
  *Development*: the tools probe v2 was built and sized on the development-only deployment
  `dev-gpu-p4-b256` ([data/v0.1.1-dev-tools-probe.jsonl](data/v0.1.1-dev-tools-probe.jsonl));
  it never appears in an evaluation table.
  *Evaluation*: the controls and faults below, with seeds 1000 and up (v0.1.0 used 0 and up).
* **Fresh held-out configurations.** Four correct deployments (`heldout-*`) were added for this
  study and used nowhere else: not in calibration, not in development, not in v0.1.0. They test
  whether calibrated thresholds generalize to benign changes nobody tuned against: flash
  attention off, 3 slots with a large batch, continuous batching off, CPU with 2 slots and
  8 threads.
* **If evaluation led to a fix,** the fix would be recorded in [decisions.md](decisions.md),
  the code re-frozen, and the affected scenarios re-run with new seeds and a new output
  directory; the rows that exposed the problem would stay in [data/](data/) next to the new ones.
  The harness refuses to mix rows produced under different configurations (decision D14).

## v0.1.0 study (historical)

Raw per-repetition data:

* full study, second run: [data/validation-results.jsonl](data/validation-results.jsonl)
* sampler-probe v3 re-validation: [data/validation-sampler-v3-results.jsonl](data/validation-sampler-v3-results.jsonl)
* full study, first run: [data/validation-v1-results.jsonl](data/validation-v1-results.jsonl)

**Three runs, and why.** The first full run exposed a sampler-probe misattribution on a Q2_K
deployment ([appendix](#appendix-first-run-sampler-probe-v1)). The probe was fixed (v2) and the
whole study was re-run with the same calibration; that second run is the **Results** section.
It showed the same class of misattribution through a different sampler case, which led to
sampler v3. Because v3 changes only the sampler probe, it was re-validated with a sampler-only
run on the GPU deployments ([section](#sampler-probe-v3-re-validation)); the other five probes'
results stand from the second run.

Reproduce with `parity inject-faults run --out runs/validation` (resumable),
`parity inject-faults run --out DIR --probes sampler.conformance --scenarios ...` for a
sampler-only run, and `parity inject-faults summarize --out runs/validation`.

### Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | AMD Ryzen 5 5600H (12 threads), 7.1 GB RAM, AMD RX 6500M 4 GB (Vulkan), no CUDA |
| Software | Python 3.12.3, torch 2.15.0+cpu, transformers 5.22.1, llama.cpp b12128 (prebuilt Vulkan and CPU) |
| Model | Qwen3-0.6B |
| Reference | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` at revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, HF transformers, fp32, CPU |
| Targets | llama.cpp GGUFs built by `llama-quantize` from one BF16 file (`unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF@50968a4`) |
| Suite | `core` (all six probes), `core-v1` data, familywise alpha 0.05, claimed context 4096 |
| Machine load | A single user's laptop. Light editing, a few short test runs and one low-priority (`nice 19`) Docker image build happened while the study ran, so the wall-clock figures are "laptop under light concurrent use", not an isolated benchmark |

**Prompt cache.** In the second run, the CPU control and eight fault scenarios ran with
llama.cpp's default 8 GiB host prompt cache; it drove the machine into swap, so the remaining
scenarios (both GPU controls and the three quantizations) ran with `--cache-ram 0`
(decision D12). Each scenario uses one setting throughout. The second run was also
interrupted once by a machine reboot (after repetition 4 of `control-gpu-p1-smallbatch`) and
resumed with `parity inject-faults run`, which skips finished repetitions; the remaining
repetitions of that control used a fresh server process with the same configuration.

**Backends.** GPU deployments run on the RX 6500M through Vulkan (the server log line
`offloaded 29/29 layers to GPU` is asserted at start-up); CPU deployments use the CPU build.

#### Calibration (benign deployments only)

Thresholds were calibrated *only* on two correct deployments that differ in benign ways:
`benign-gpu-p4` (BF16, GPU, 4 slots) and `benign-cpu-p4` (BF16, CPU, 4 slots). Resulting
thresholds ([data/validation-calibration.json](data/validation-calibration.json)):

| metric | benign-gpu-p4 | benign-cpu-p4 | threshold (max x 2) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| mean KL lower bound (nats, upper CI) | 6.75e-06 | 6.78e-05 | 1.36e-04 |
| greedy divergence hazard (Wilson upper) | 0.00474 | 0.00788 | 0.0158 |
| tool-trigger disagreement (Wilson upper, 0/24) | 0.138 | 0.138 | 0.276 |

#### Controls (held out from calibration)

Correct deployments configured *differently* from the benign ones, so the false-positive rate
is measured on configurations the thresholds never saw. Each repetition is a full `core` run
with a different seed.

| control | configuration | repetitions |
|---|---|---:|
| `control-gpu-p2` | BF16, GPU, 2 slots, ctx 8192 | 10 |
| `control-gpu-p1-smallbatch` | BF16, GPU, 1 slot, `-b 128 -ub 64` | 10 |
| `control-cpu-p1-t4` | BF16, CPU, 1 slot, 4 threads | 3 |

#### Injected faults (3 repetitions each)

| fault | how it is produced |
|---|---|
| `template-llama3` | real: `--chat-template llama3` |
| `template-nosystem` | real: custom template file without a system role (llama.cpp polyfills the system text into the user turn) |
| `quant-q8_0`, `quant-q4_k_m`, `quant-q2_k` | real: GGUF quantizations of the same BF16 weights |
| `ctx-reduced` | real: `--ctx-size 2048`, one slot, while 4096 is "claimed" |
| `topk-ignored`, `topp-ignored`, `temperature-ignored`, `temperature-x1.5` | **simulated**: a proxy rewrites the request fields before they reach an otherwise correct server (llama.cpp has no switch for these bugs) |
| `silent-truncation` | **simulated**: a proxy keeps only the last 6000 characters of the final user message |

### Sampler probe v3 re-validation

In the second run the sampler column shows 1/3 for Q2_K: sampler v2 reported `top_k=5`
violations (2.0% of samples) on a deployment whose sampler is correct. Measured directly, Q2_K's
reported log-probs differ by up to 0.058 nats between identical requests (BF16: 0.0016), as much
as the 0.077-nat gap between that context's 5th and 6th token. Sampler v3 judges every sample
against the distribution reported in its own response (decision D13). It was re-run alone on the
GPU deployments, with the same per-probe alpha it has in the full suite (alpha/4). The sampler
should report DEVIATION exactly for the four sampler faults and PASS for everything else
(quantization changes the model, not the sampler).

<!-- TABLES_SAMPLER_V3:BEGIN -->
| Scenario | Sampler fault? | Should report | Reps | Sampler DEVIATION | Median sampler requests | Median seconds |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fault-quant-q2_k | no | PASS | 10 | 0/10 | 3504 | 36 |
| fault-topk-ignored | yes | DEVIATION | 3 | 3/3 | 4904 | 82 |
| fault-topp-ignored | yes | DEVIATION | 3 | 3/3 | 6204 | 98 |
| fault-temperature-ignored | yes | DEVIATION | 3 | 3/3 | 4604 | 80 |
| fault-temperature-x1.5 | yes | DEVIATION | 3 | 3/3 | 3304 | 58 |
| fault-quant-q4_k_m | no | PASS | 3 | 0/3 | 7004 | 56 |
| fault-quant-q8_0 | no | PASS | 3 | 0/3 | 7004 | 67 |
| control-gpu-p1-smallbatch | no | PASS | 5 | 0/5 | 7004 | 98 |
| control-gpu-p2 | no | PASS | 5 | 0/5 | 7004 | 98 |
<!-- TABLES_SAMPLER_V3:END -->

**Result.** Sampler v3 reported DEVIATION for all 12 sampler-fault repetitions and for none of the
26 others (16 quantized deployments, 10 correct controls), testing all seven cases on Q2_K in every
repetition. The first 12 repetitions ran with 4 concurrent requests, the rest with 2 and a 120 s
cool-down because of laptop temperatures (decision D13); the seconds column mixes both.

### Interpretation

**False positives.** None of the 23 control runs (three held-out correct configurations:
GPU with 2 slots, GPU with 1 slot and small batches, CPU with 1 slot and 4 threads) was flagged,
and no individual probe raised a false flag. With 23 runs that bounds the false-positive rate at
14.8% (95% upper limit); it does not show the rate equals the nominal 5%. The controls differ from
the calibration deployments in slots, batch sizes, threads and (for part of the second run) the
host prompt cache, so they test whether the calibrated thresholds generalize to unseen benign
changes, not just repeats.

**Detection.** All 11 faults were detected in 3 of 3 repetitions (with 3 repetitions the 95%
lower limit is 29%; the point is that no fault was missed, not a precise power estimate).

**Attribution.** The probes that fire match the cause, which is what lets a report say *how*
behaviour differs:

* Template faults are caught by the template probe (deterministic token-count mismatch) and by
  the long-context probe's accounting, which since the second run correctly names a constant
  offset as a template difference, not truncation. The distributional and greedy probes, which
  use raw token-id prompts without a chat template, correctly stay silent.
* Sampler faults are caught only by the sampler probe. Ignored temperature is also caught by the
  greedy probe, because greedy (temperature 0) requests then sample at temperature 1.
* Silent truncation and a reduced context window are caught only by long-context accounting
  (fewer reported prompt tokens; rejection inside the claimed window).
* Quantization is caught by the distributional probe in every repetition, including Q8_0, whose
  measured KL lower bound (1.3e-3 nats, docs/data/distribution-live.json) is about 9x the
  calibrated threshold (1.36e-4). The greedy probe catches Q2_K and Q4_K_M every time but is at
  the edge of its power for Q8_0 (2/3 in the first run, 0/3 in the second): Q8_0's divergence
  hazard (0.028) lies between the calibrated benign rate (0.016) and the SPRT's alternative
  (0.079). Whether a near-lossless quantization *should* count as a deviation is a policy choice
  expressed by the threshold; with thresholds calibrated on benign variation, Parity reports it.
* The sampler column's 1/3 for Q2_K is a misattribution by sampler v2, explained and re-validated
  in the next section; the verdict for that repetition was still a correct DEVIATION.
* The tool probe flagged none of these faults. Its calibrated benign disagreement rate (0.28,
  the Wilson upper bound of 0/24) leaves little power with 24 prompts; its useful checks here are
  the deterministic ones (raw tool markup, invalid tool names, schema violations), which none of
  these faults triggered. This is a real limit of v0.1.

**Cost.** A correct deployment needs the full suite: about 6,900 requests, a median of 106-155 s
on the RX 6500M and 659 s on the CPU. With `--fail-fast`, faults stop as soon as one probe
decides: template faults after 7 requests, truncation and reduced context after 16, ignored
temperature and Q2_K/Q4_K_M after 52, Q8_0 after 355 (one look of the distributional probe), and
sampler faults after 2,800-6,600 (the sampler runs last because it is the most expensive).

### Appendix: first run (sampler probe v1)

Same calibration, scenarios and repetitions, run with sampler probe v1. In one of three Q2_K
repetitions the sampler probe reported a deviation for `top_p=0.6` (2.4% of samples outside the
nucleus). The sampler itself was correct: the server's own log-probs jitter slightly between
requests, and that context's cumulative mass sat within a hair of 0.6, so the boundary token
moved in and out of the nucleus. The overall verdict was still a correct DEVIATION (the
distributional and greedy probes caught the quantization), but the *attribution* was wrong.
v2 places `top_p` per context away from cumulative-mass boundaries (decision D11); a regression
test reproduces the situation.

### Limits of this study

* One small model, one reference, one serving stack (llama.cpp). Nothing here says how the
  probes behave on a 70B model, on vLLM or on a hosted provider; those adapters are
  implemented against documented formats and fixture-tested, not validated live.
* Faults marked *simulated* are bugs injected by a request-rewriting proxy; real servers that
  have those bugs could differ in detail.
* Repetitions of one deployment share the same server process and the same reference results;
  they are independent in the sampler's randomness and in the seed, not in the deployment.
* Controls give a confidence interval, not a guarantee: with N runs and zero false positives the
  upper 95% bound on the false-positive rate is about 3/N.
